text:
Maya: quick sync — i'm proposing a new initiative to codify model lifecycle ramp-downs and customer "flightpaths" across hosted / dedicated / private. goal: make migrations predictable + low-friction, with clear gates and incentives. thoughts?

Sam: +1. need concrete rollout gates and canary plan. otherwise ops will get burned.

Carlos: agree. we also need a reproducible benchmark harness (golden prompts + perf matrix) before any mass migration. who owns it?

Maya: product will own the spec and overall policy; eng-ml to own the harness. early draft of acceptance gates below — please comment.

```
Acceptance gates (draft):
- perf: p95 latency on 2k token synthetic <= 250ms for hosted profiles
- cost: per-token cost delta <= 15% vs current pinned model (weighted by common lengths)
- quality: pass rate >= 95% on core eval prompt set (semantic accuracy + hallucination tolerance)
- robustness: no new high-severity regressions on customer-stored prompts
- safety: zero critical safety regressions on blocked prompt suite
- infra: fallback path available (compatible variant) with <2s extra routing latency
```

Priya: from sales/customer asks — we need >= 90 days deprecation notice for large customers, and an optional 6mo pin for billed customers. also migration credits are a big win (e.g., 3 months free or discount).

Jordan: cs can do migration playbooks and a checklist for customers. need telemetry hooks (call_id, prompt_hash, model_version) exposed to customer support for debugging.

Sam: ops/eng notes: propose canary rollout cadence: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 24h observation windows. rollback triggers: error rate spike > 2x baseline or quality metric drop > 3 percentage points. include automated rollback policy in the runbook.

Carlos: benchmark infra should run across 3 hardware profiles (small, med, large) and include embedding/semantic tests + latency/cost tradeoffs. we should publish a short report per model:
- p50/p90/p95 latency
- tokens/sec throughput
- embedding cosine stability
- eval pass rate per prompt category

Maya: i want to introduce the concept of "flightpaths" — customer-facing migration lanes with clear obligations:
- QuickOpt-in lane: user flips opt-in, automatic migration; 30-day rollback window; no cost credits.
- Assisted lane: product & cs assist migration, includes 3 months migration credit and a dedicated support plan for the cutover.
- Long-pin lane: customers pay a premium to pin a specific minor version for up to 6 months (managed by dedicated infra), after which we revisit.

Priya: those lanes map well to commercial asks. Sales will push Assisted for enterprise customers. need clear eligibility criteria (usage threshold, SLA tier).

Sam: operational needs for Long-pin: we must reserve capacity (dedicated pool) or implement fair-share throttles; otherwise pinned customers will impact global throughput. add reserved capacity cost calc to the spec.

Maya: agreed — include cost modeling table and example invoices in the spec. also we should add a short comms template for each lane that CS/Sales can reuse.

Jordan: i'll draft the comms + playbook checklist. quick checklist item: require an internal sign-off before pin expiration 30 days prior so customers get a nudge.

Carlos: on benchmarks — we should include a small open prompt-set for regressions and a seeded fuzzing harness to catch edge hallucinations. i'll add dataset pointers in the PR.

Sam: runbook action items: routing fallback implementation, auto-rollback lambda, canary dashboard alerts. i'll put a runbook PR up by wednesday.

Maya: action list i captured — please confirm:
- Sam: rollout ops runbook + automated rollback policy (due Wed)
- Carlos: benchmark harness + small regression prompt-set (due Thu)
- Priya: commercial lane definitions + migration credit proposal (due Fri)
- Jordan: customer comms + cs playbook (due Fri)
- Maya: spec doc (policy + acceptance gates + cost model + flightpaths) and console copy (due next Tue)

Sam: confirmed.

Carlos: confirmed.

Jordan: confirmed, will also prepare 2 customer-facing one-pagers.
